title: Contingent staffing bucket plan & price elasticity scan (2026)
summary: Working workbook that prototypes a short-term contingent staffing bucket (contractors + temp hires) to bridge Q3–Q4 2026 demand while testing three pricing sensitivity paths. Objective: quantify marginal burn, unit economics, and necessary headcount flex levers under alternative demand and price-change hypotheses.
sheet_1_notes: Context: Product spike (customer A pilot) could raise token volume by +20–60% for 6–9 months. We have limited ability to accelerate fulltime hiring; propose a contingent staffing bucket (3 tiers: support, infra ops, ML-serving) to buy time. This sheet mixes headcount phasing, cost curves, and a simple price-elasticity scan to show tradeoffs. Not final — needs SRE and Head of Sales assumptions for conversion rates.

budget_sensitivity_scenarios:
Scenarios: 
- Base: no price change, demand +20% sustained for 6 months. Add 15 contingent FTE months total. Marginal monthly burn (contingent comp + onboarding + tooling) ~ $380k. 
- Upside (price +10%): demand +30%; assume 20% conversion to paid volume; reduce need for contingent by 25%; net ARR uplift estimated. 
- Downside (price -10%): demand +40% (elastic), but revenue per token falls; require additional 20% contingent capacity; marginal burn increases by ~30%.
Each scenario runs through a 9-month window; sheet calculates cumulative cash delta vs baseline and headcount runway impact.
assumptions:
- Average contractor fully-loaded rate includes taxes and benefits-ish (1.25x billing) applied to base rate.
- Onboarding costs: one-time ramp cost = 0.5 * monthly rate for first month for contractors.
- Token unit economics baseline taken from hosted API median: revenue per 1k tokens = $0.45, marginal cost per 1k tokens = $0.09.
- Conversion assumptions: Sales-led conversions at 5–20% depending on pilot quality; scenario-specific modifiers in pricing matrix.
- No change to Dedicated reserved capacity pricing commitments in these scenarios (we assume existing commitments absorb baseline).
questions_and_next_steps:

4) If upside scenario materializes, propose a small Headcount-to-FTE conversion window: convert top 40% of contractors to full-time in Q1 2027 (plan sketch included).
